name: esp32c3
comment: An ESP32-C3 on its development board: a single-core RISC-V chip with Wi-Fi and Bluetooth. ESP-IDF is the platform here rather than a bare linker script, because the chip's flash is reached through a partition table and its radio needs the IDF's own startup, so the build is a CMake ESP-IDF project and the HAL implementations are robohub-esp32's.

flash.comment: the app partition of the flash: ESP-IDF writes the program here and reads it back through the cache at 0x42000000, which is the address the linker script uses

irom.comment: the flash seen through the instruction cache

flash.comment: the offset is the app partition's, and an IDF project also writes a bootloader and a partition table
